llm.summary: The skill's requirements, install methods, and runtime instructions align with its stated purpose (a CLI for unified customer data); nothing requested appears unrelated, but the CLI can modify agent configuration and the API key grants access to sensitive customer data, so proceed with standard operational caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (customer-data CLI) matches requirements: the skill only requires the outlit binary and OUTLIT_API_KEY. The declared npm package and Homebrew formula both produce the outlit binary — these are proportional to the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the outlit CLI for queries and to use 'outlit setup' which can auto-detect and configure MCP and specifically 'outlit setup openclaw'. That is within the integration scope but implies the CLI may modify agent configuration or write stored credentials/config — be aware of these side effects before running automated setup commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installers are npm (@outlit/cli) and a Homebrew tap (outlitai/tap/outlit). These are standard distribution channels for a CLI; no arbitrary download URLs or extract-from-unknown-host steps are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only OUTLIT_API_KEY is required and is declared as the primary credential. That is appropriate for a CLI that accesses unified customer data. Note: the auth lookup mentions 'stored config' — the CLI may read or write local config to persist credentials, which is expected but means stored credentials must be treated as sensitive.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forced-always and allows user invocation; model invocation is permitted (default). The notable persistence risk is that the CLI's 'setup' command can configure MCP/agent integrations and write stored config — this can change agent environment/configuration and should be reviewed before running in production or granting the API key broadly.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and appropriate for integrating the Outlit CLI, but the OUTLIT_API_KEY gives broad access to customer data and the 'outlit setup' command can modify agent configuration. Before installing: (1) verify the npm package and Homebrew tap are official and match your org's policy; (2) provision an API key with minimal required scopes and store it in a secrets manager rather than pasting in shells; (3) avoid running 'outlit setup --yes' in production until you know exactly what files/config it will change (test in an isolated environment); (4) review Outlit docs for what 'setup openclaw' modifies and which agents/credentials it will configure; (5) if you allow autonomous agent invocation, restrict which agents can call this skill because it can access sensitive customer context.
